posts.style: Design & Aspiration · The Outdoor Kitchen as the Dining Room
posts.alt: A Carmel Valley, San Diego backyard at golden hour behind a Mediterranean stucco home with a terracotta tile roof: a stone-veneer outdoor kitchen island with built-in grill and pizza oven niche, a travertine terrace with a long teak dining table under a wood-beam pergola, a lit stone fireplace wall, potted olive trees and lavender, with neighboring homes visible close by on both sides and beyond the wall
posts.hook: The best table in the house is the one with the kitchen right behind it.
posts.caption:
The new year is when most people start imagining a different way to use their yard. The answer is usually simpler than a bigger yard: put the cooking, the table and the fire in one conversation.

Here the kitchen island sits at the edge of the terrace so the cook is never cut off from the table. A pizza oven niche gives the wall some life, and the fireplace gives the evening somewhere to go. Travertine underfoot keeps it cool and warm-toned, and the planting stays Mediterranean and soft: olive, lavender, rosemary.

The selections:
• Eldorado Stone veneer outdoor kitchen island with Lynx built-in grill
• Belgard travertine-look paver terrace
• wood-beam pergola over teak dining
• stone-veneer fireplace wall
• olive, lavender & rosemary in terracotta pots · FX Luminaire lighting

Planning a kitchen that feels like part of the house? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Neighborhood · Driveway & Curb Appeal · The Slate-Pattern Drive
posts.alt: The front of a 1950s ranch-style home in Clairemont, San Diego, at golden hour: a wide driveway of stamped concrete in an ashlar slate pattern in warm grey-tan with a charcoal border band, a matching entry walk, a planter bed of ornamental grasses and agave with a Japanese maple, a mature street tree, and neighboring homes close by on both sides and across the street
posts.hook: A driveway can carry the character of a whole house, and it can do it in a single material.
posts.caption:
Clairemont's mid-century ranch homes have good bones and long, low rooflines. The front yard's job is to match them with something quiet and well made.

This drive is stamped concrete in an ashlar slate pattern, with the warm grey-tan tones of real stone and a charcoal border that draws the edge in one clean line. The walk picks up the same pattern, so the approach reads as one gesture from the street to the door. Ornamental grasses and agave keep the planting low and in scale, and a single Japanese maple gives the bed its focal point.

The selections:
• stamped concrete in an ashlar slate pattern, grey-tan blend with charcoal border
• Mexican feather grass, agave & Japanese maple
• Kichler bronze path lights

Want the front of the house to hold its own? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Process Carousel · Property Walk to Built
posts.alt: Four-slide SDLR process carousel of one Santee ranch-home backyard between neighboring houses: the existing yard at the property walk with a cracked slab, a failing old patio cover and dry lawn, the full 3D design render with louvered pergola, outdoor kitchen, fire pit and curving turf, a hand-rendered design drawing of the same layout with client details left unlabeled for privacy, and the finished build at golden hour
posts.hook: Here's how a backyard goes from tired to built, without a single guess along the way.
posts.caption:
Most yards we start with are ordinary in the best way: a normal lot, close neighbors, a slab that has seen better years. What changes it isn't a bigger idea. It's an order of operations.

Swipe through how our design process works, start to finish:

1. The property walk: we start with what's actually there. The cracked slab, the old cover, the grade, the sun and the fence lines.
2. The 3D design: the whole space modeled so you can see the pergola, the kitchen, the fire and the lawn in place, and change anything before it's real.
3. The drawing: every edge, level and planting resolved on paper so the crew builds exactly what you approved. Client details stay private.
4. The build: and it matches, because nothing was left to be figured out in the field.

The selections:
• Belgard paver patio
• StruXure louvered pergola
• Eldorado Stone kitchen island with Lynx built-in grill
• stone-veneer fire pit with curved seat wall
• SYNLawn turf · olive, agave & lavender in raised planters

Want to see your own yard in 3D before anything gets built? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Coastal Pool · Fire · The Hillside Terrace
posts.alt: A Point Loma hillside terrace at golden hour behind a white coastal-contemporary home with large glass doors: an infinity-edge pool with an ivory porcelain deck stepping down the slope, a black steel pergola with a linear gas fire table and low cushioned seating, stacked-stone retaining walls, olive trees and agave, a sliver of ocean in the distance, and neighboring homes visible close by on both sides and down the hillside
posts.hook: On a slope, every level is a room. The trick is making them feel like one.
posts.caption:
Point Loma yards rarely give you flat ground, which is exactly why they reward a careful plan. The hillside here becomes three rooms in sequence: a pool deck to step out to, a fire table under a pergola to settle into, and a quiet planted edge that lets the ocean do the rest.

The ivory deck is continuous with the interior floor line so the glass doors feel like a threshold rather than a wall. Stacked stone holds the slope and gives the terraces their rhythm. The water runs to the edge so the horizon becomes part of the pool.

The selections:
• Belgard porcelain pool deck in ivory
• infinity-edge pool with tile and stone coping
• StruXure steel pergola in black with a linear gas fire table
• stacked-stone retaining walls
• olive trees & agave · FX Luminaire lighting

Have a slope and a view? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Trust & Difference · Aerial · The Plan You Can See From Above
posts.alt: A drone aerial at golden hour of a Black Mountain Ranch, San Diego family backyard between neighboring tile-roof homes: a freeform pool with a stone-veneer spa, a paver patio with a pergola and lounge seating, a round stone fire pit with curved seat wall, raised planters with olive trees, and fenced neighboring yards close by on all sides with hills beyond
posts.hook: A good yard is decided from above, long before anyone picks up a shovel.
posts.caption:
This is the view we like to start from: the whole lot at once, every room accounted for before anything is built.

A freeform pool with a spa at one end, a lounge under a pergola, a fire pit with a curved seat wall where the evening ends up. On an ordinary Black Mountain Ranch lot with close neighbors, it works because each space has its own square footage and nothing is left to be figured out in the field.

That's how we work. Your project manager is your one point of contact from the first walk to the last, with no hand-offs in between. And ten months after the build is finished, we come back and walk it again with a fine-toothed comb. By design, not by dispatch. References available on request.

The selections:
• freeform pool with stone-veneer spa
• Belgard paver patio with Trex pergola
• stone-veneer fire pit with curved seat wall
• olive trees in raised planters

Starting the year with a plan for your yard? DM “DESIGN”.
